name: EvoPrompt
executive_summary: Genetic algorithm over prompts. Treats prompts as individuals in a population, applying crossover and mutation operators to evolve higher-performing prompts over generations.
description: EvoPrompt initializes a population of prompt variants, evaluates each on a validation task, and applies genetic operators: (1) Selection — keep top-performing prompts, (2) Crossover — combine parts of two high-performing prompts, and (3) Mutation — randomly alter words or phrases in a prompt. This evolutionary process continues for a fixed number of generations or until performance plateaus.
when_to_use: Prompt optimization where the search space is large and unstructured.
When gradient-based or Bayesian methods are impractical.
Tasks where prompt structure matters more than individual word choice.
when_not_to_use: When evaluation is too expensive for large populations over many generations.
When prompts must remain interpretable (evolution can produce gibberish).
When a strong initial prompt already exists (evolution may degrade it).
known_pitfalls: Population size and generation count require careful tuning.

primary_source.authors: Guo, Wang, Guo, Li, Song, Tan, Liu, Bian, Yang
primary_source.title: EvoPrompt: Connecting LLMs with Evolutionary Algorithms Yields Powerful Prompt Optimizers

variables.name: task
